newsitem.title: USA: Jobless claims down in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Jobless claims down in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell in the latest week, the government said on Thursday in a report that analysts said reflected a stable labour market.
The Labour Department said 331,000 people filed first-time claims for unemployment insurance in the week ended Nov. 2, down from 342,000 claims in the previous week.
Economists said the report suggests labour markets remain tight, bolstering the theory that consumption in the fourth quarter might be strong.

"It indicates that we have a persistent tightness in the labour market and that should continue indefinitely since we're likely to get a bit stronger consumer numbers in the fourth quarter," said Lee Youngdahl, vice-president and an economist at Aubrey G. Lanston and Co. Inc.

The new data brought the average weekly rate of new claims in the past four weeks to 333,500, up from 331,250 in the prior week. Economists consider the average to be a more reliable indicator of employment trends than the weekly numbers.

"That four-week moving average has been holding right around 330,000 for a while now," said Greg Jones, economist at Briefing.com, in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. "I think we have to realise that small moves in claims in the range of 10,000 to 20,000 really are not very helpful in predicting job growth."

The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond lost half a point and its yield climbed to 6.66 percent from 6.62 late Wedesday. But economists said the fall was mostly tied to an overnight slump in the dollar, triggered by bearish comments by a Japanese finance ministry official.

Overall benefit rolls rose to nearly 2.49 million in the week ended Oct. 26, the latest period for which those data were available. That was up from 2.44 million in the previous week, the department said.
The department said 12 states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Oct. 26, the latest period for which those data were available.
Among states with the largest increases were Michigan with 8,049, Ohio with 6,993, California with 3,829, Pennsylvania with 2,751, Illinois with 2,407 and New York with 2,026.

Michigan reported automobile industry layoffs associated with the General Motors strike in Canada. Ohio reported layoffs in various industries. California cited layoffs in the food and agricultural industries.
Pennsylvania cited layoffs in the food, rubber, plastics and fabricated metals industries, and in manufacturing.
Illinois had layoffs in the trade and service industries and in manufacturing, while New York linked the increase to layoffs in the transportation equipment industry.
Mississippi had a 1,012 drop in initial claims exceeding 1,000 in the Oct. 26 week while Puerto Rico had 1,566 fewer filings, the department said.
